Historian Gad Barnea studies the ancient texts behind the Bible, and he joins Danny Jones to argue that newly examined writings change what we know about the Bible's origins. His subject is the world of ancient Israel's neighbors, whose records have only recently become readable in full.

Barnea explains how inscriptions and documents from surrounding cultures reframe familiar stories: where ideas came from, which gods were worshipped when, and how the texts were edited over time. Jones asks the layman's questions, and Barnea answers from the sources. The claims come from active scholarship rather than fringe theory, though scholars debate them too. Listeners interested in the Bible's real ancient context, beyond both Sunday school and debunking, will find this among the most substantive episodes in the series.

Paul Rosolie is a conservationist who works in the Peruvian Amazon, protecting rainforest and filming its wildlife. With Danny Jones, he discusses the strange ancient discoveries being reported from the rainforest. They include structures and earthworks. They also include signs that large, organized societies lived where the jungle was long assumed to have been nearly empty.

Archaeology in Amazonia has genuinely changed in recent years, as lidar reveals settlements under the canopy; Rosolie adds the frontiersman's feel for what the forest hides. Jones asks about the finds and the threats, logging and mining, closing in on them. Rosolie's authority here is lived: he has spent his adult life in that forest. The episode gives listeners the romance and the science of a real frontier together, from the rare guest in this series whose mysteries can be visited.

Danny Jones hosts a debate between Ammon Hillman and exorcist Bob Larson over who the real Christ is. The episode title bills it as Antichrist against exorcist. Hillman reads old texts in Greek, and Larson casts out demons for a living.

Hillman argues the first faith was built on drugs and rites the church later hid. Larson answers from scripture and from his years at the altar of war with evil. Jones keeps the two men in the ring as they clash. Listeners get a rare, raw fight over the roots of the faith. The library holds it as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-Wl309-Mn1z0:
Why are UFOs being acknowledged now, after decades of denial? Rogan asks that timing question in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. The shift is real: pilots testify, Congress holds hearings, and agencies publish reports that once would have been buried.

The talk weighs the kind answers: better sensors, braver witnesses, and a public already primed. Then it weighs the cynical ones: distraction, budgets, and control of the story. Rogan leaves the motive open. The segment is a useful marker of the disclosure era's central riddle, posed by a host who has interviewed nearly everyone involved in it.
